text:
Minnesota led 2-0 after two periods on a pair of goals it barely earned. Danila Yurov scored on the power play on a 6% chance, and Maxim Shabanov added a second on an 11% look 1:45 later. Buffalo was already pressing in the second (0.98 expected goals to 0.83), but Jesper Wallstedt's night was just beginning. He saved 1.2 goals more than the 28 shots he faced deserved.

The third period belonged to the Sabres, who out-chanced MIN 1.54 to 0.27 in expected goals. Noah Ostlund deflected one in at 3:55, and Tage Thompson tied it at 9:38 with a snap shot. Thompson took nine shots on goal and was on the ice for 1.85 expected goals for against 0.85 against. Overtime stayed lopsided, 1.18 to 0.36 for BUF, and Zach Benson had a 47% look that Wallstedt stopped.

Owen Power finally ended it at 4:22 of overtime on an assist from Jiri Kulich and Thompson, finishing with a goal and an assist in 29:06 of ice time. Over the whole game, BUF held a 4.18 to 1.98 edge in expected goals and a 64 to 48 edge in shot attempts, which is why the model gives Buffalo an 83% chance to win a replay. The comeback from two goals down was the fair outcome for the way the game was played.
